title: When the Colony Breaks Again
premise: Ivo Voss, an insurance investigator who specializes in 'impossible accidents' along the silent trade routes between the warring colonies of Meridian and Ceres Reach, is aboard a freighter when gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds. In those nine seconds, every person on his ship briefly remembers a life they never lived — and Ivo realizes he is one of thousands of memory-echoes seeded by a pre-war experiment meant to force empathy between the colonies. Hunted by both governments who want the experiment erased, Ivo must carry the original message — nine seconds of shared memory recorded in a dying scientist's neural lattice — to the neutral jump relay before the window closes, knowing its broadcast will either shatter the war or detonate it. He delivers it; the colonies, forced to feel each other's grief for nine seconds, stand down, and Ivo chooses to keep his borrowed memories rather than have them wiped, finally belonging to two worlds at once.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to stories about people caught between systems that refuse to speak. She writes from a converted pilot house overlooking a cold northern harbor.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Ivo Voss. Ivo investigates a cargo hauler's impossible decompression on the Meridian–Ceres route, cataloguing small human details of a crew that no longer exists. Establishes his loneliness, his methodical empathy, and the cold politics of two colonies that stopped speaking five years ago. Emotional beat: competent isolation masking grief he won't name.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Mid-jump, gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds. Ivo experiences an entire alternate life — a daughter, a garden on Ceres, a war he died in — then finds his crewmates weeping over memories that aren't theirs. The freighter's AI logs the event as a system-wide anomaly. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; the first crack in his certainty about who he is.

chapters.title: Claims Against the Sky
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Docking at Meridian, Ivo files the anomaly as an accident claim and discovers forty-seven identical filings across the system — all flagged and sealed by both governments within hours. A Meridian intelligence officer, Sefa Okonkwo, offers him money to forget what he saw. Emotional beat: the investigator becomes the investigated; paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: The Lattice
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, with interludes from Dr. Amara Sen's dying log entries. Following sealed-claim patterns, Ivo locates retired neuroscientist Amara Sen, architect of the pre-war 'Concordance' experiment that seeded echo-memories into colonists' genomes. Dying, she entrusts him her neural lattice containing nine seconds of unfiltered shared memory — and the coordinates of the neutral jump relay. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance; a stranger's purpose becomes his own.

chapters.title: What Both Sides Want Buried
chapters.summary: POV alternating Ivo and Sefa. Sefa reveals the truth she's sworn to bury: both governments knew about Concordance and let the war run because shared memory would end their leverage. She offers Ivo asylum if he surrenders the lattice. He refuses and runs. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed — even his pursuer is a prisoner of the lie.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. On the run aboard a smuggler ship, Ivo bonds with a patched-together crew — each carrying their own echo-memories they've hidden for years. Found family forms around shared secrets rather than shared history. They plan the run to the relay through a contested debris field. Emotional beat: warmth earned in danger; the theme of found family crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Debris Field
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The run through wreckage of the war's first battle goes wrong when a Ceres patrol traps them. The crew's echo-memories — soldiers on both sides remembering dying at each other's hands — nearly cause them to turn on one another. Ivo talks them down using Sen's lattice as proof. Emotional beat: memory as weapon and wound; the cost of carrying the message made visceral.

chapters.title: Sefa's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Ordered to destroy the freighter, Sefa instead experiences her own suppressed echo — a sister lost on the other side — and defects mid-burn, feeding Ivo the patrol's approach vectors. Her captain marks her for death. Emotional beat: the antagonist's arc completes; loyalty to truth outweighs loyalty to power.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At the relay, with minutes before the window closes and both fleets converging, Ivo must physically interface with the lattice — risking dissolution of his own identity into nine seconds of everyone's grief. The crew holds the docking ring against boarding parties while he connects. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice framed not as death but as choosing to hold more than one life.

chapters.title: After the Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, epilogue six months later. The broadcast ripples through both colonies; fleets stand down as millions share the same grief simultaneously. Peace talks begin in the relay's shadow. Ivo, keeping his borrowed memories, opens a small claims office serving both worlds — investigating accidents no longer, but reuniting echo-carriers with each other. Emotional beat: resolution; identity as something chosen, family as something built.
